headlines.article_text: Stock market today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, US, November 20, 2026. Brendan Mcdermid | Reuters U.S. stock futures were marginally lower on Tuesday night, following a slide in tech stocks during the regular session that drove the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite lower. Traders also looked ahead to fresh inflation data. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures lost 68 points, or 0.1%, while S&P 500 futures declined 0.2%. Nasdaq-100 futures traded down 0.3%. In Asia, South Korea's Kospi plunged 4.49% on Wednesday, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.41%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.41%. Ambarella plunged 37% in U.S. extended trading after the designer of low-power AI vision and video chips issued fourth quarter revenue guidance of $70 million to $75 million. That fell massively short of the $112 million analysts polled by LSEG were expecting. Wall Street is coming off a losing session for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite , after tech stocks gave back some of their gains from the prior session as Nvidia sank and Anthropic fell below its IPO price. The broader index fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq slid 1.5%. On the other hand, the 30-stock Dow which has less exposure to tech, climbed more than 400 points, or 0.9%. The choppy trading action was just the latest in a volatile month. Even before the ouster and reinstatement of Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and Democrats' sweep in the midterm elections, investors were deliberating the future of the artificial intelligence build-out amid a worsening macroeconomic outlook. "Let's remember that the sell-off in the AI ecosystem predated the news about Huang and Nvidia," Liz Ann Sonders, chief investment strategist at Schwab Center for Financial Research, told CNBC's " Closing Bell " on Tuesday. "The concerns about capex, the data center build-out, the spread between the cost of capital and return on invested capital, the bifurcation that's happening in the market now between sort of profitable segments of the market and unprofitable," she added. "I think that is the bigger, more aggregate story." Traders are turning their attention toward the personal consumption expenditures price index for October, due on Wednesday morning. Economists polled by Dow Jones see the headline reading rising by 0.3% for the month and 3.8% annually. The company's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand. In opening remarks, Dell said it has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours from delivery. In this article DELL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Dell Technologies demonstrates its technology at its exhibition booth during the 15th Smart Tech Korea exhibition at COEX in Seoul, South Korea, on June 10, 2026, as visitors explore the company's displays and exhibits. Chris Jung | Nurphoto | Getty Images Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter. Dell shares rose in extended trading. Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates: EPS : $9.45, adjusted, versus $6.59 expected Revenue : $54.94 billion, versus $49.32 billion expected Dell said that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $7.50 per share on $53.61 billion in revenue. The company's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand. The company's largest line is its infrastructure solutions group, or ISG, which makes AI servers and systems, often based around AI chips from companies like Nvidia and AMD . ISG sales during the quarter were $41.97 billion, topping an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion. Of that, $22 billion was for AI-optimized servers, up 291% on an annual basis. ISG now accounts for 85% of Dell's total revenue. "We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth," said Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and COO, in a statement. He said that Dell has 7,500 customers buying AI servers. In prepared remarks, Clarke said that Dell has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours of delivery. "That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably," Clarke said in the prepared remarks published by Dell. The company also raised its forecast for AI-servers in the coming fiscal year to $78 billion, versus $74 billion expected. The company says it has a backlog of $132.3 billion in AI server orders it is working through. "Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power," Clarke said on an earnings call with analysts. The company also sells laptops and PCs, in a group it calls CSG, or client services group. It reported $12.89 billion in sales, which was below LSEG expectations of $14.33 billion. The overall PC market has been getting whacked of late, with some estimates calling the lull the worst ever, as rising memory prices have led to higher device prices and consumers are choosing to hang on to their old laptops longer. Dell said that it had authorized $25 billion in share repurchases, and that it had spent $4.9 billion in the third quarter on share repurchases and dividends. Dell shares are up over 135% so far in 2026.
